card.summary: no service and no account; a Rust library and the boringtun-cli binary

free_tier.stated: no service and no account; a Rust library and the boringtun-cli binary

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume; ingress: none

record.tooling: cargo install boringtun-cli; Rust library for embedding
record.chaining: sits under a WARP client or under a wrapper; it composes with cloudflare-warp and adds nothing to a hosted tunnel by itself.
record.binding_note: boringtun adds no path of its own: it encrypts and decapsulates over UDP exactly as the protocol specifies, so a UDP block stops it
record.reliability_note: README warns the master branch is mid-restructure; use the crates.io releases
record.confidence_note: the verdict is about egress, not quality: boringtun is load-bearing inside the official Cloudflare WARP apps, and is the substrate a wrapper needs

evidence.proved: "an implementation of the WireGuard protocol designed for portability and speed", deployed on millions of iOS and Android consumer devices
"It implements the underlying WireGuard protocol, without the network or tunnel stacks" - the library half does no I/O at all
release boringtun-cli-0.5.2 published 2022-07-20; last push 2026-06-29; 7230 stars
"Boringtun is currently undergoing a restructuring. You should probably not rely on or link to the master branch right now"

record.notes: Userspace WireGuard implementation in Rust. Operates as a protocol implementation and network interface, not as a transport encapsulation proxy or hosted service. Used in Cloudflare WARP client software.

extras.wg_detail: boringtun-cli is a userspace WireGuard executable that takes the standard interface configuration, so a normal .conf drives it
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume
extras.transit_note: carries a user's own traffic to whatever peer it is configured against
extras.hosting_requirement: none beyond the device, but no far end either: it needs a WireGuard peer and speaks only UDP to it
